known_issues.mooneye_detection: Mooneye/SameSuite/Wilbertpol ROMs signal via the Fibonacci register fingerprint (B=3 C=5 D=8 E=13 H=21 L=34 pass, all $42 fail) at an LD B,B breakpoint. Since GB-1 the core's mooneye adapter (cores/gb/src/test_channel.cpp) turns that into REG + END 1/1 / END 0/1 code=66 in the VELOCE-RESULT/1 file, so these are real verdicts. This item (SH-7 gb) flipped every remaining result_detection: serial entry that resolves through it to result_detection: file, channel: mooneye, matching the actual source of the verdict. It is still a Tier C (register-heuristic) channel: 153 tests use it, which is exactly why result_policy stays legacy for gb (validate_configs.py --strict rejects Tier C channels). GB-4/GB-5 rebuild the suites to emit CHECK/END over the serial channel themselves and GB-8 flips these entries to channel: serial, rom_variant: veloce, after which result_policy: strict becomes reachable.
known_issues.blargg_onscreen_only: RESOLVED (GB-3): halt_bug.gb and interrupt_time.gb do write blargg's $A000 block, but their header declares MBC1+RAM with RAM size 0, so no cart RAM was mapped. They now run as rom_variant veloce builds with only $0149 set to 8 KiB (tests/roms-src/gb/blargg/).
known_issues.mem_timing2_serial_crash: RESOLVED (GB-3): the 0x80 byte that crashed the harness's stdout decode was not serial output. It was the CGB flag at $0143 leaking into the cartridge title the core prints ('02-WRITE_TIMING\x80'): cartridge.cpp compared a signed char against 0x80. Fixed in the core; mem_timing-2 is scored from the $A000 block.
known_issues.cpu_instrs_combined: The combined cpu_instrs.gb / mem_timing.gb print no aggregate serial verdict (MEASURED); the individual ROMs do, and are used instead.
known_issues.cpu_02_interrupts: RESOLVED: cpu_instrs 02-interrupts PASSES through the blarggtext adapter (26 frames, measured 2026-09-27). The old 'no serial Passed at 8000 frames' note came from the DEBUG-stdout era; the entry is expected: pass now.
known_issues.pixel_fifo_scanline_based: Core README states the pixel FIFO is scanline-based, not dot-accurate. Expected to fail the hardest mid-scanline PPU tests (Mealybug, Wilbertpol, intr_2_mode0_timing_sprites).
known_issues.mbc2_unsupported: Core README lists only None/MBC1/MBC3/MBC5; MBC2 acceptance ROMs cannot pass until MBC2 is implemented. bits_ramg specifically now resolves as unverified (RUNS), not known_fail: see its test-level note (SH-7 gb honest-detector fix). (No MBC3-specific Mooneye acceptance ROMs exist; MBC3 RTC is covered by rtc3test in the bundle but not yet wired here.)
known_issues.visual_refs_unpopulated: All screenshot-crc reference_hash values in visual_test_suites (acid2, Mealybug) are empty, so those SKIP. They are non-scoring by design (plan section 11, Q1).
known_issues.model_selection: The core picks DMG or CGB from header byte $0143 only ($80/$C0 -> CGB) and has no per-test model override. Two groups therefore run on the wrong hardware and stay known_fail until one exists (core + testkit gap, not a measurement gap): Blargg oam_bug ($0143=$80, run as CGB, which has no OAM bug; the ROMs verify the DMG bug) and the Mooneye misc/ CGB-hardware ROMs ($0143=$00, run as DMG). Note the two oam_bug ROMs that check for the ABSENCE of corruption (3-non_causes, 6-timing_no_bug) pass trivially in CGB mode: they count as PASS, but they do not demonstrate DMG behaviour.
known_issues.gbmicrotest_scope: GB-3 enumerates the GBMicrotest categories named in the plan (timer/div, dma, hblank_int_scx, halt, lcdon_to_stat, VRAM/OAM lock): 212 of the 482 ROMs whose source ends in a test_end2-family macro (the $FF80-$FF82 triple). The other 270 reporting ROMs (poweron_*, win*, sprite*, line_153*, stat_write_glitch*, lyc/oam/vblank interrupt edges, int_* nops/incs, mbc1_*) are left for GB-7/GB-8. 31 ROMs contain no result macro (testbenches, display-only probes, the empty stub temp.gb) and cannot be scored.
known_issues.result_policy_strict_blocked: result_policy stays "legacy" (SH-7 gb). validate_configs.py --strict (result_policy: strict) rejects any test whose channel/require_channel is a Tier C heuristic (mooneye here, r12 on gba); 153 of this file's 448 tests still resolve through the mooneye LD B,B fingerprint adapter (12 Mooneye acceptance suites, wilbertpol_ppu, and the 5 SameSuite/APU groups), because GB-4/GB-5 have not yet patched those suites' source to emit CHECK/END over the real serial channel. No expected_checks values were added by this item either: every channel currently in use (mooneye/a000/hram/blarggtext) synthesizes exactly one END (1/1 or 0/1) per ROM with no per-ROM CHECK line, so there is no per-ROM check count to know yet; expected_checks only becomes meaningful once a suite emits multiple real CHECK lines per ROM (GB-4/5/6/7/10).
known_issues.samesuite_apu: SameSuite APU (46 ROMs, channel: mooneye) measured 0/46 on 2026-09-27; 44 are expected: pass and count as real failures. The 46 had been known_fail since before any of them could produce a verdict (they were RUNS under the stdout era), which after GB-1 silently hid measured failures from the headline. Upstream apu/README.md: all pass on real CPU-CGB-E; the two it lists as failing even on SameBoy/CGB-D (channel_4_freq_change, channel_1_sweep_restart_2) stay known_fail with that reason.
known_issues.known_fail_policy: Every expected: known_fail entry carries a per-test notes reason or points at a known_issues entry (review follow-up 2026-09-27). A measured failure without a documented hardware/WIP reason is expected: pass and counts against the headline.
